Both walks retain a 256 MiB response cap, and events and heartbeats carry one collection ID plus expected/actual output counts.
* **Scalable Assurance Issue collection:** Issue collection uses `GET /dna/data/api/v1/assuranceIssues` with a fixed 24-hour window, 25-record pages, stable ordering, and pacing below the documented 50 requests/minute. Count, identity, byte, deadline, and complete-before-publish checks remain mandatory. The default interval is 1,800 seconds; the 17,989-Issue regression is exactly 720 pages with an 898.75-second pacing floor after page one. Existing high-volume 300-second stanzas must be increased. Missing device identity uses deduplicated point lookups for up to 10 devices or one verified bulk inventory walk above that threshold. Only endpoint absence selects the bounded legacy collector, which reports `status=recovering` because its unpaged list cannot prove completeness.
* **Shared controller protection:** Every Catalyst Center API input now has an 80%-of-interval poll deadline, request timeouts clipped to the remaining budget, a 30-second maximum `Retry-After` with jitter, deterministic process-start staggering, and a controller-scoped request governor shared by modular-input processes on the same Heavy Forwarder. Device Health reserves its documented 20-requests/minute slots; Site and current Security Advisory calls reserve their documented 100-requests/minute slots. The controller identity is hashed in the local coordination filename; credentials and payloads are never stored there.
* **Security Advisory and Compliance N+1 removal:** Both collectors take one bounded, count-verified device inventory snapshot and join device/site metadata in memory. Security Advisory uses the current 500-record paginated advisory and affected-device APIs, derives severity totals from the completed current snapshot instead of calling the sunset aggregate API, reconciles every relationship walk with `deviceCount`, caps advisory/device relationships and response bytes, and fails the whole cycle on an incomplete relationship. Older controllers use the bounded sunset API family and report `status=recovering`. Compliance now bounds both status/detail walks and no longer performs two enrichment calls per device.
* **Bounded secondary snapshots:** Site Topology, Client, and Audit Logs now share repeated-page, page-count, record-count, response-byte, and fail-closed guards. Site Topology events include snapshot ID, sequence, and expected count; all three inputs report pagination and output completeness. Application Traffic, SWIM, and Network Health also reject malformed, oversized, or over-limit single responses and enforce the shared output deadline.
* **Compact change checkpoints:** Issue, Security Advisory, and Client Health store SHA-256 content fingerprints in 16 batched KV Store ledger documents instead of reading and writing one full checkpoint document per record. A bounded compatibility migration preserves the first 1,000 legacy states; any excess is emitted at most once and then uses the ledger. Stale hashes are removed on a rotating 45-day schedule, and the ledger advances only after event output succeeds.
* **Capacity-aware Device Health setup:** The production default and large-fleet baseline are now 900 seconds. A controller inventory above 1,000 devices at a shorter interval emits `capacity_warning=true`; Data Collection Health uses the same 15-minute freshness expectation, and the 900-second setting remains a coverage ceiling because the source query covers only the previous 15 minutes.
* **Splunk Cloud-safe collection health:** The active React Data Collection Health dashboard now derives scheduled-report, process, and resource status exclusively from indexed events, structured poll heartbeats, and accelerated data. It no longer runs SPL `rest` searches for local server or input configuration, which also avoids incorrectly treating search-head configuration as the Heavy Forwarder collector configuration. Automated tests keep its expected intervals aligned with `default/inputs.conf`.
* **Accurate duplicate and error diagnostics:** Dataset-specific SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring source paths now collapse to their parent input stanza before duplicate detection, so one consolidated input is not mistaken for many inputs. SD-WAN Health device discovery treats a short final page as normal completion and fails closed on malformed, repeated, or oversized walks. TA internal-log parsing retains bounded 100 KB/1,000-line tracebacks, and oversized vendor bodies preserve both their opening context and final root-cause text.
* **Workload-aware sizing chapter:** The operator guide now separates Catalyst Center API polling, syslog, NetFlow/IPFIX/HSL, and Splunk ingest/search capacity instead of routing the general sizing link to a NetFlow-only subsection.
* **ITSI input planning example:** A worked five-cluster, 26,000–29,000-device example sizes Device Health, Issue, Security Advisory, and Site Topology separately, documents uneven regional distribution, and uses a measured regional-HF starting layout.
* **Evidence boundary made explicit:** Heavy Forwarder tuning improves forwarding and queue reliability but does not accelerate serial Catalyst Center pagination or remove API rate limits. The preferred 500-record Device Health path cuts the five-cluster average from roughly 520–580 requests to 22–24 requests across both walks, and the Assurance Issue path removes the old N+1 enrichment design. These are still post-fix pilot configurations—not production capacity guarantees. Intervals above 900 seconds are not a general Device Health remedy because that input requests only the prior 15 minutes.

##### API input polling intervals

* **Editable SD-WAN intervals:** Administrators can change the polling interval when editing any of the five SD-WAN API inputs. Site/Tunnel Details now uses the same editable numeric interval control as the other SD-WAN inputs.
* **Existing guardrails preserved:** A positive integer is still required. Saving a value below the recommended interval displays the existing **Interval below recommended value** warning with **Cancel** and **Save anyway** choices.
* **Cyber Vision parity verified:** All seven Cyber Vision API input forms include an editable interval, send it in the edit payload, and use REST handlers that accept the update.

##### SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring

* **REST-only consolidated input:** **SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring** lets one stanza select several catalog dataset IDs and a device scope; authentication and collection stay on the SD-WAN Manager REST API with no device shell access.
* **Stable event contract:** Every record uses `cisco:sdwan:realtime` and carries `dataset_id`, `dataset_label`, `monitoring_category`, `record_kind`, `endpoint_path`, `target_device_id`, `hostname`, `device_model`, `site_name`, `system_ip`, `tags`, `vmanage_host`, `collection_time`, and `schema_version`. Splunk `host` uses the lowercased device hostname when available. Dataset-aware eventtypes and tags map BFD sessions, routing sessions, hardware alerts, and performance records to appropriate CIM categories without creating hundreds of sourcetypes.
* **One-call inventory enrichment:** One bounded `/dataservice/device` read per poll supplies the Devices-table identity fields for every selected dataset and powers the device selector. Enrichment is an in-memory system-IP lookup, not an API call per event or device.
* **Category-filtered dataset selection:** Choosing a Real-Time Monitoring category narrows the dataset menu to that category. Existing selections from other categories remain visible only while selected so changing filters cannot silently remove them.
* **Readable Cisco category names:** The category picker uses the catalog's human-readable Cisco domain labels instead of reconstructing names from machine slugs, preserving terms such as `DOT1x`, `IPv4 FIB`, `PPPoE`, `QoS`, and `SD-WAN`.
* **Splunk-safe vendor fields:** Real-Time response keys cannot shadow Splunk metadata or TA-owned knowledge fields. Cisco's row-level `index` is emitted as `vendor_index`, leading `@` is removed from keys such as `@rid` (emitted as `rid`), and any future collision is retained with a `vendor_` prefix. The calculated `app=cisco_sdwan` field remains available for CIM and knowledge-object classification. This advances the Real-Time event envelope to schema version 2.
* **Complete managed-device inventory:** Real-Time Monitoring lists and can target the full reachable Manager inventory, including SD-WAN Manager, SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), and SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) controllers as well as WAN Edges. The generic API Endpoint Collection remains WAN Edge-only.
* **Bulk first, bounded fan-out:** All-device collection uses documented bulk state APIs for BFD Sessions, BGP Neighbors, Control Connections, Control Local Properties, Control WAN Interfaces, and Hardware Alarms. Other selected datasets fan out with a shared ten-request-per-second pace, at most five workers, bounded pagination, bounded records, and three attempts for rate-limit or server failures.
* **Workload qualification:** The runtime estimates initial requests before data collection and limits the plan to 80% of the interval's paced request capacity, with a hard cap of 10,000 initial targets. The six-dataset recommended selection plans 5,006 initial requests for 5,000 devices at 900 seconds: one inventory call, five bulk calls, and 5,000 BFD History calls. Larger selections must be split, narrowed, or given a longer interval.
* **History and partial failures:** History datasets use a per-input, per-dataset/device checkpoint with a five-minute overlap window and bounded recent hashes, preserving late arrivals while suppressing repeat records. Successful devices are still indexed when other dataset/device requests fail; the poll heartbeat reports `recovering` with success/failure and request metrics.
* **No duplicate endpoint path:** Every catalog entry classified as Real-Time Monitoring is hidden from the generic SD-WAN API Endpoint Collection picker and rejected by its modular input. Existing generic custom sourcetypes remain unchanged for compatibility, while this dedicated input intentionally uses one stable sourcetype.

##### SD-WAN collection guidance

* **Consolidated real-time collection:** **SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring** selects several datasets in one stanza, supports one, selected, or all reachable managed devices including controllers, and emits one stable sourcetype with dataset identity fields.
* **Bulk-first large-fleet behavior:** Six recommended datasets fit the 900-second admission guardrail for a representative 5,000-device fleet because five use documented controller-wide bulk state calls and BFD History uses bounded per-device fan-out.
* **Scale and failure guardrails:** Shared request pacing, five workers, bounded retries, pagination and record caps, and an 80%-of-interval workload budget prevent an unbounded **Select all** pattern. Partial target failures preserve successful records and set the heartbeat to `recovering`.
* **Checkpointed BFD history:** A per-input, per-dataset/device checkpoint with a five-minute overlap suppresses repeated history while preserving bounded late arrivals.
* **Duplicate prevention:** Real-Time Monitoring paths are removed from the generic endpoint picker and rejected by the generic modular input. Both collectors enforce exact backend catalog IDs/paths, and neither exposes arbitrary URLs, device actions, or shell execution.
* **Audit-log scope clarified:** The Audit Logs guidance now distinguishes SD-WAN Manager administrative and configuration activity from general device shell-command or operating-system process telemetry that the Manager does not expose through the audit-log API.
* **ZBFW HSL recommendation clarified:** The guide now explicitly recommends High Speed Logging through NetFlow for production ZBFW pass/drop/inspect coverage because firewall text syslog is rate-limited and may not preserve every matching record under sustained load.
* **HSL and syslog coexistence documented:** The guide now explains that HSL does not disable ordinary IOS-XE or UTD syslog, but becomes the primary export path for configured ZBFW event classes. Equivalent `%FW-*` duplicates must not be assumed, HSL pass notifications can still follow a configured rate limit, and Unified Logging changes pass/drop behavior on IOS XE SD-WAN 17.16.1a and later.

info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk

releases.notes:
#### Highlights

* **Product family alignment:** Renamed the package to **Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk**. The existing `TA_cisco_catalyst` application ID, sourcetypes, stanzas, and compatibility identifiers remain unchanged.
* **Guided NetFlow configuration:** Added a five-step Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN NetFlow workflow that checks dependencies, guides the NetFlow v9 or IPFIX v10 choice, configures the local Stream receiver, confirms the destination index, and requires canary validation.
* **Protocol-aware guidance:** Added separate guidance for NetFlow v9 with High Speed Logging and IPFIX v10 with Unified Logging. Suggested ports do not overwrite saved receiver settings.
* **Safer Stream activation:** Destination-index changes are saved and verified before a disabled Stream definition is enabled. Missing or unverifiable Stream dependencies block unsafe index operations.
* **NetFlow collection health:** Added NetFlow status to the Data Collection Health overview and a dedicated view for freshness, volume, processing hosts, pipeline rates, destination indexes, and indexed hosts.
* **Stable migration contracts:** Added self-contained transition eventtypes so current and retained Catalyst Center, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Generic Custom API, and Cisco Identity Services Engine data remain searchable without renaming or reindexing historical events.
* **Improved syslog collection:** Added supported TLS listener options, corrected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN firewall framing and fallback routing, and expanded native Unified Threat Defense message parsing.
* **Improved collection health:** Corrected Catalyst Center device matching and report status, expanded migration-aware health searches, and improved Cisco Identity Services Engine multipart and alarm processing.
* **Application Setup improvements:** Added a focused full-width workspace, a draggable layout, release badges, consistent product names, sourcetype explanations, and visible diagnostic log levels.
* **Build and metadata integrity:** Made source `app.conf` authoritative for the package label and aligned macOS, Linux, and Windows packaging behavior.

#### Upgrade notes

* Splunk Enterprise 9.4.0 or later is the supported platform floor.
* New events use the documented stable sourcetype families. Historical events retain their original sourcetypes; use the supplied transition eventtypes across both.
* Do not rename or reindex historical data during the migration.
* Install the required Splunk Stream packages and **Cisco Enterprise Networking NetFlow Add-on for Splunk 4.0.0** on their documented deployment tiers.
* Validate one representative controller or edge before expanding collection across a large environment.
* After upgrading the companion app, rebuild the `Cisco_Catalyst_App` acceleration summaries.

**Important for upgrades:** Before migrating saved searches or alerts, review the legacy dynamic-sourcetype upgrade checks in the User Guide included with the TA.

##### What's New modal

* **Release notes surface automatically:** Each release now opens a polished What's New modal inside the add-on, with a compact section navigator and a direct link to the full User Guide.
* **Explicit per-user suppression:** Closing the modal normally hides it only for the current page visit, so the release notes return the next time the add-on opens. Selecting **Do not show again** before closing stores the suppressed version for the signed-in Splunk user; a newer release appears automatically, and the modal can still be reopened from Application Setup.
* **Restart-free, cluster-consistent preference updates:** The user-scoped `ta_cisco_catalyst_ui.conf` now has an explicit reload trigger and Search Head Cluster replication declaration, so saving **Do not show again** no longer requests a restart and remains consistent across cluster members.
* **Single release-note source:** The modal renders the bounded **Current release at a glance** subsection from this User Guide Markdown, so its concise announcement and the full guide cannot drift into separately maintained release-note files.

##### Application Setup release badges

* **Current release callouts:** Input Type menus now show compact **New!** and **Enhanced!** badges beside this release's highlighted inputs across Catalyst Center, Cyber Vision, SD-WAN, and ISE. A selected highlighted input keeps its badge in the closed control.
* **New NetFlow workspace:** The SD-WAN **NetFlow** tab now carries the same compact **New!** badge so operators can spot the new listener, dependency, and destination-index workflow immediately.
* **Release-only metadata:** Badges come from one release-maintained index and are display-only. They do not rename input types, change saved values, issue API requests, or alter collection behavior, and can be updated or removed independently before a future release.

##### Guided SD-WAN NetFlow workspace

* **Requirements first:** Step 1 checks all four required Stream and Cisco packages before the operator changes a listener or SD-WAN Manager configuration. The live result is limited to the current Splunk Web node and tells the operator where remote collector and indexer placement must be verified.
* **Five numbered steps:** The workflow continues through protocol choice, listener configuration, destination-index confirmation, and one-edge canary validation with explicit Back and Next actions.
* **Visible prerequisite guard:** A live preflight now warns when App for Stream (1809) or Stream Wire Data (5234) is missing, disabled, or unverifiable. Destination-index requests and the Stream configuration link remain paused until App for Stream is ready, preventing an absent custom endpoint from appearing as a generic 500 error. The warning distinguishes the current-node check from Wire Data placement that must also be verified on every indexer.
* **Progressive disclosure:** Only the active task is shown, and optional listener tuning, exporter allowlists, capacity guidance, and configuration-file details remain collapsed until needed.
* **Saved forwarder identity explained:** A populated **Stream Forwarder ID** is loaded from the existing `stream_forwarder_id` value in `Splunk_TA_stream/local/inputs.conf`; the page neither generates nor hard-codes it, and a blank value continues to let Stream use the host name.
* **Current product terminology:** Customer-facing UI and guide text now use **Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager**; **vManage** remains only in explicit legacy labels, literal compatibility signals, fields, URLs, and old release names.

##### UI build dependency security

* **Dependabot remediation:** The React build and development toolchain now resolves the patched Babel, Webpack development server, WebSocket, proxy, YAML, CSS, URI, glob, and related transitive packages required by the repository's security advisories.
* **Unused parser removed:** The unused `image-size` development dependency was removed, eliminating its unpatched image-parser paths without changing the shipped UI or runtime React/UCC libraries.
* **Deterministic security floor:** Targeted npm overrides keep transitive packages above their fixed versions while preserving the existing Splunk React/UCC runtime contract and reproducible `npm ci` builds.

##### Catalyst Center scheduled-report namespace

* **Report sourcetypes aligned with Catalyst Center:** Newly collected scheduled reports now use `cisco:dnac:inventory:report`, `cisco:dnac:compliance:report`, and `cisco:dnac:report` instead of the older `cisco:catalyst:center:*` report namespace.
* **Dual-read transition eventtypes:** `cisco_dnac_inventory_report`, `cisco_dnac_compliance_report`, and `cisco_dnac_report` each search the exact current and previous sourcetypes. `cisco_catalyst_center_reports` searches all three report families. Historical events are neither renamed nor reindexed.
* **Visible migration contract:** Application Setup displays an amber migration warning plus **Current sourcetype**, **Previous sourcetype**, and **Transition eventtype** columns. Data Collection Health uses the umbrella eventtype so current and retained report data remain visible together.
* **Readable migration table:** The report description now lives inside each row's expandable **More info** panel, leaving the three migration identifiers enough room to remain readable in the default split-panel layout.
* **Report identity remains stable:** `report_name`, `report_type`, `report_category`, `cisco_catalyst_host`, and `collection_timestamp` continue to identify the report definition, family, controller, and snapshot time. Arbitrary report rows are not assigned a payload-specific CIM tag without a validated schema.

##### Resizable Application Setup workspace

* **Drag-resizable product and configuration panels:** Add Input pages now default to a 70/30 product-information/configuration layout and provide a center splitter that can be dragged directly with a mouse or pointer between bounded 30/70 and 70/30 layouts. Left/Right and Home/End keys provide an accessible alternative, double-click restores the 70/30 default, the current ratio remains visible, and narrow viewports continue to stack the panels automatically.

##### Stable Generic Custom API sourcetypes

* **One sourcetype per product family:** Generic Custom API events now use `cisco:dnac:custom`, `cisco:sdwan:custom`, `cisco:ise:custom`, or `cisco:cybervision:custom` instead of creating a sourcetype for every selected REST endpoint.
* **Endpoint identity remains searchable:** Every custom event includes a normalized, bounded `endpoint_name` plus the cataloged `endpoint_path`, so searches and dashboards can select an endpoint without expanding sourcetype cardinality.
* **Identity fields explained in context:** The expandable **More info** panel for every product's Generic Custom API sourcetype now explains how `endpoint_name` groups a selected operation, how `endpoint_path` preserves its configured catalog route, and when SD-WAN adds `target_device_id` for device-scoped collection.
* **CIM-safe shared metadata:** The stable families retain the add-on's universal `vendor`, `product`, `vendor_product`, and `app` fields. Payload-specific CIM mappings remain with dedicated inputs because arbitrary endpoint JSON does not share one truthful data-model contract.

##### Stable ISE policy and analytics sourcetypes

* **One policy family:** Newly collected RADIUS and TACACS+ policy sets and authorization rules use `cisco:ise:policy`. The bounded `policy_protocol` field identifies `radius` or `tacacs`; `policy_record_type` identifies `policy_set` or `authorization_rule`; `endpoint_name` and `endpoint_path` preserve the originating Open API surface.
* **One analytics family:** General, registry, hardware, applications, and full endpoint report rows now use `cisco:ise:analytics`. `report_type` identifies the bounded report family and `report_name` preserves the source filename.
* **Dual-read transition eventtypes:** `cisco_ise_policy` and `cisco_ise_analytics_reports` search their current family plus retained history. The protocol/record and report-specific eventtypes shown in Application Setup provide exact old-and-new searches. Historical events are not renamed or reindexed.
* **Visible migration contract:** The ISE product card displays an amber migration warning plus **Current sourcetype**, **Previous sourcetype**, and **Transition eventtype** columns. Descriptions and identity-field guidance remain available through each row's **More info** panel.
* **CIM-safe scope:** Both current families expose universal `vendor`, `product`, `vendor_product`, and `app` fields. Policy snapshots are configuration state, not authentication transactions, and variable analytics report rows are not assigned a payload-specific CIM tag without representative schema validation.

##### Data Collection Health sourcetype migration roll-up

* **Current-family health:** Data Collection Health rolls retained Catalyst Center, endpoint-derived Custom API, SD-WAN firewall/access/syslog, and ISE policy/analytics sourcetypes into their current canonical families before calculating freshness, status, volume, and chart series. Historical events remain unchanged in the indexes.
* **No false retired-feed outages:** Retained names no longer age into separate Critical rows after their current replacement is healthy. The retired ISE Security Group event feed is excluded because the current Security Group Tags workflow refreshes KV Store data rather than indexing a replacement event sourcetype.
* **Physical evidence remains available:** Data Quality, scheduled-report evidence, and onboarding **Processed Sourcetypes** retain physical names for migration and routing diagnosis. The Cyber Vision catch-all `cisco:cybervision:custom` family is now included in Data Quality and uses the same 60-minute health expectation as the other Custom API families.
* **NetFlow ingest health:** A fifth Overview status card and a dedicated NetFlow tab now track the Stream-owned `stream:netflow` path. The tab shows freshness and selected-window license volume, a 30-minute arrival trend, processing-host throughput and pipeline evidence, destination-index activity, and the top indexed host values without scanning raw high-volume flow events.
* **Accurate SD-WAN text-syslog output list:** Application Setup now lists only the five current text-routing destinations. It excludes the separate REST Audit Logs sourcetype and retained per-message history, while explaining that firewall output is conditional and modern Unified Logging delivers covered security events as `stream:netflow`. Transition eventtypes continue to search historical names.

##### SD-WAN NetFlow guidance

* **Reproducible SD-WAN telemetry runbook:** Application Setup and the User Guide now distinguish the exact live-tested v9, v10, and syslog paths from conditional signal families, explain that the listener form manages receiver 0 only, and add a stop-on-drift Manager preview and canary gate.
* **Production sourcetype contract:** Splunk Stream continues to index production NetFlow and IPFIX events as `stream:netflow`; this TA does not change that metadata and supplies bounded search-time CIM knowledge for the Stream-owned events.
* **Four-step NetFlow setup:** The SD-WAN **NetFlow** tab now behaves as a compact setup flow instead of one long page: choose NetFlow v9/HSL or IPFIX v10/Unified Logging, configure the listener, confirm the destination index, and validate packages and packets. Back/Next controls keep only the current task visible, while optional listener restrictions remain behind a clearly labeled control.
* **Corrected Unified Logging cutover:** The guidance no longer assumes that UTD text syslog remains available in parallel after Unified Logging is enabled. It directs operators to capture a bounded UTD syslog baseline before cutover and validate the corresponding IPFIX records afterward.
* **Local Stream listener setup:** The tab can now read and save the local UDP NetFlow listener managed by Splunk Stream through native authenticated Splunk configuration endpoints. It detects up to 64 IPv4/IPv6 addresses assigned to the host so an operator can select one or enter a different valid bind address. It writes the owning app's `Splunk_TA_stream/local/inputs.conf` and `streamfwd.conf`, validates the app URL, bind IP, UDP port, sender filters, and a bounded 1–32 decoder-thread setting, and never changes `streamfwdlog.conf` or restarts Splunk. The form explains exactly what the save action changes and clearly marks the documented user-run restart required after saving.
* **Inline destination-index editing:** Each Stream-owned NetFlow definition can now change its destination index directly in the Cisco add-on. **Edit index** stays beside the value it controls and opens a responsive full-width editor so the index, sourcetype, status, and actions remain aligned at narrower widths. The editor defaults unset definitions to `default`, reuses the same visible non-internal index choices as the other input forms, changes only the definition's `index`, and verifies the saved value without altering its fields, filters, mode, ownership, or Stream-managed sourcetype. Definitions owned by another app remain read-only here and link to Splunk App for Stream.
* **Single production Stream definition:** The destination-index panel now promotes `cisco_hsl_cisco_hsl_netflow` as the authoritative Cisco HSL/IPFIX definition when it is installed and enabled. Disabled, generic, or comparison definitions remain available under **Other Stream definitions** for troubleshooting instead of appearing as equal production choices. If multiple definitions are enabled, the page warns that overlapping filters can duplicate indexed flow records and directs operators to keep exactly one intended production definition enabled.
* **Stream HEC setup:** The same tab checks HTTP Event Collector readiness and, when authorized, creates or enables the managed `streamfwd` HEC input in one click. Splunk retains the generated token; the Cisco add-on does not display it, log it, or store it in browser state.
* **Live deployment dependency checks:** The tab identifies the Stream Forwarder, App for Stream, Wire Data, and conditional Cisco Catalyst Enhanced NetFlow packages, shows live installed and latest-version status, and offers filtered **Install** or **Update** links alongside each Splunkbase listing. Missing, disabled, or unverifiable App for Stream status now pauses destination-index access instead of surfacing a generic endpoint error; missing Wire Data is called out for both search-head and indexer placement. It configures only the local listener and HEC readiness; SD-WAN Manager export and the applicable Stream definition remain separate deployment steps.
* **Configured Inputs lifecycle:** A saved receiver now appears as **NetFlow Listener** in the SDWAN group on Application Setup. Operators can enable or disable it, jump directly back to the NetFlow editor, or delete both managed Stream stanzas from the same actions menu. Every listener mutation retains the explicit user-run restart boundary.
* **Stream-owned NetFlow sourcetype:** The SD-WAN product card and NetFlow tab identify `stream:netflow` as the unchanged production sourcetype and direct operators to the stable `cisco_netflow` eventtype for CIM-scoped searches.
* **Stable CIM eventtype:** `eventtype=cisco_netflow` searches `sourcetype=stream:netflow NOT event_name=netFlowOptions` and carries the `network` and `communicate` tags. Saved searches, alerts, dashboards, and data-model validation should use this contract.
* **CIM 8.6 Network Traffic normalization:** Bounded search-time mappings cover production `stream:netflow` for NetFlow v9 and IPFIX v10. They normalize exporter identity, endpoints, interfaces, ports, IP/transport versions, direction, duration, actions, policy/rule identity, users, TCP flags, VLANs, and existing Stream byte/packet/application fields. Options metadata remains excluded from the Network Traffic eventtype.
* **Reliable Stream configuration namespace:** Listener reads, creates, updates, toggles, and deletes now use the explicit `nobody/Splunk_TA_stream` REST namespace, so a missing stanza cannot be created accidentally under the signed-in user's current app namespace.
* **Dedicated-index and clock-skew verification:** NetFlow validation now follows the configured `netflow` destination index, verifies Cisco decoding through enterprise fields rather than contradictory base searches, and includes an index-time canary for exporters whose clocks are wrong.
* **Measurement-led capacity planning:** Removed the unsupported fixed per-device volume estimate and fixed ingest multiplier. The guide now derives daily volume and p95 collector load from a representative pilot and requires UDP-loss, template, CPU, queue, and indexing-lag evidence before production qualification.
* **Manual fallback boundary:** Direct `streamfwd.conf` editing and App for Stream mode repair are now labeled advanced fallback procedures. Application Setup remains the primary listener and destination-index workflow.

##### User guide navigation and search

* **Readable Heavy Forwarder tuning table:** The tuning reference now fits the guide viewport without horizontal scrolling, keeps the 30-second load-balancing default as the starting value, and separates the single-pipeline baseline from a measured two-pipeline override that requires CPU, memory, network, and queue headroom.
* **Descriptive browser tabs:** Application Setup, Add Input, Data Collection Health, and User Guide tabs now include the Cisco Catalyst Add-on name so they remain identifiable beside other Splunk pages. The guide sets its final browser title explicitly so Splunk does not append a platform-version suffix.
* **Reliable search navigation:** Pressing Enter or **Next** immediately after changing a guide query applies the current query and navigates to the first visible document result, excluding the print-only contents list. **Clear** removes the query and returns the reader to the top of the guide.
* **Compact navigation rails:** **Jump to a task** is collapsed by default, and the **On this page** rail no longer repeats the operator-directory links as duplicate headings.
* **Executable sizing search:** The Device Health event-size example now opens with `index=main` instead of a literal index placeholder; administrators replace `main` with their Cisco data index.
* **Executable SD-WAN upgrade check:** The legacy-sourcetype audit now opens with `index=main`; administrators are told to replace `main` with the index that holds their SD-WAN syslog.
* **Copy-only migration example:** The SD-WAN before/after sourcetype example remains syntax-highlighted and copyable without presenting a misleading **Open in Search** action for its mutually exclusive alternatives.
* **Customer-controlled time ranges:** Routine User Guide SPL examples rely on the Splunk time picker. The NetFlow clock-skew recovery canary is the documented exception: operators select **All time**, then use a bounded recent index-time window so bad exporter timestamps cannot hide fresh ingestion.
* **Consistent index scope:** Customer-facing SPL examples use executable index names instead of wildcard or literal placeholder values.
